html:
Turkey is the republic that spans Anatolia and a corner of south-eastern Europe, with its capital at Ankara and its largest city at Istanbul. It was founded in 1923 from the core of the Ottoman Empire. The map shows it from 1938.

After the Ottoman defeat in the First World War, Mustafa Kemal (Atatürk) led a war of independence that drove out Greek, French and other forces and tore up the plan to divide Anatolia. The republic was founded in 1923. Atatürk abolished the caliphate, closed religious courts, adopted a Swiss-based civil code, replaced Arabic script with the Latin alphabet and gave women the vote. The price was one-party rule and harsh treatment of the Kurds, who make up the largest minority.

Turkey stayed neutral for most of the Second World War, then joined NATO in 1952. Multiparty elections began in 1950, but the army took power in coups in 1960, 1971 and 1980. In 1974 it invaded northern Cyprus. Since 2003 Recep Tayyip Erdoğan has led the country, first as prime minister and then as president.
